hypotheses.title: SingleProviderHelper._calculateOutputLPAndProtocolFee unchecked overflow — no guard unlike FixedHelper counterpart
hypotheses.mechanism: SingleProviderHelper._calculateOutputLPAndProtocolFee (line 170-171) performs `unchecked { amountInAfterFees = reserveAmountIn + lpFeeAmount; }` without any overflow guard. The identical function in FixedHelper (lines 1067-1072) includes an explicit check: `if (amountInAfterFees < lpFeeAmount) { revert FixedPool__Overflow(); }`. When sqrtPriceX96 is near MIN_SQRT_RATIO (~2^32) and amountOut is ~2^127 (max uint128 reserve), calculateFixedOutput returns reserveAmountIn ~2^255. With poolFeeBPS >= 5001, lpFeeAmount = mulDivRoundingUp(2^255, 5001, 4999) > 2^255, and their sum overflows uint256. The wrapped amountInAfterFees becomes near-zero, making the swap appear to cost almost nothing for full reserves. The AMM's _validateProtocolFees at lines 1660-1663 catches this downstream because totalFees > wrapped amountIn always holds when overflow occurs, but SingleProviderHelper itself silently produces corrupted values — a defense-in-depth gap exploitable if AMM validation is ever relaxed or bypassed.
hypotheses.grounded_in: Confirmed SingleProviderHelper line 170-171 has unchecked addition with no overflow guard. FixedHelper lines 1067-1072 has explicit guard. When MIN_SQRT_RATIO price causes calculateFixedOutput to produce ~2^255 reserveAmountIn, fee sum overflows.
hypotheses.exploit_sketch: Attacker: (1) SingleProvider pool with hook returning sqrtPriceX96 near MIN_SQRT_RATIO (4295128739). (2) Pool has ~2^127 output token reserves, poolFeeBPS = 5001. (3) Calls swapByOutput for full reserves. (4) calculateFixedOutput returns reserveAmountIn ~2^255. (5) lpFeeAmount = mulDivRoundingUp(2^255, 5001, 4999) ~= 2^255.0003. (6) unchecked sum overflows uint256, wrapping to near-zero. (7) AMM's _validateProtocolFees catches it but pool type returns corrupted state — if validation bypassed, attacker drains reserves for 0 cost.
hypotheses.victim: AMM protocol and pool token holders — attacker could drain reserve tokens paying near-zero input if downstream validation is bypassed.

hypotheses.title: AMMModule._validateProtocolFees DoS on FixedPool swapByInput→swapByOutput fallback path via fee formula mismatch
hypotheses.mechanism: AMMModule._validateProtocolFees (lines 1654-1677) checks `poolProtocolFees >= expectedProtocolFee`. hypotheses.title: FixedHelper.collectFees compounds four independent Q128 truncations, permanently locking LP fees
hypotheses.mechanism: FixedHelper.collectFees (lines 577-580) calculates fee0 and fee1 by performing four independent integer divisions by Q128: `fee0 = (growthA - lastA) / Q128 + (growthB - lastB) / Q128` and same for fee1. Each division truncates up to Q128-1 units in the X128 domain. With four independent divisions, a position collecting small fees loses up to 4*(Q128-1) X128-units per collection event. A single `(sum_of_growth_deltas) / Q128` would lose at most Q128-1 total, meaning the current implementation loses up to 4x more. These tokens are tracked in AMM feeBalance but are never distributable to any LP.

hypotheses.title: FixedHelper._crossHeight fee growth outside flip under rapid height oscillation shifts fee attribution between LP positions
hypotheses.mechanism: FixedHelper._crossHeight (lines 2015-2019) performs the Uniswap V3-style fee growth outside flip: `feeGrowthOutside = feeGrowthGlobal - feeGrowthOutside`. This relies on modular uint256 arithmetic — crossing the same height boundary twice with no fee accrual restores the original value. However, when a height boundary is crossed and uncrossed in rapid succession AND fee growth globals increase BETWEEN the two crosses (from the swap fees themselves), the flip captures the inter-cross fee growth in the feeGrowthOutside value. For positions spanning exactly one side of the oscillated height, `getFeeGrowthInside` will attribute fees differently. An attacker sandwich-oscillating a boundary while holding a position on the benefiting side can extract fees rightfully belonging to other LPs.
hypotheses.grounded_in: Read _crossHeight lines 2015-2019 confirming fee growth outside flip. getFeeGrowthInside reads feeGrowthOutside values in unchecked block. Oscillation pattern: cross up (flip), generate fees, cross back down (flip again with new global) — the second flip captures inter-cross fees asymmetrically.

(2) Fees from this swap increase feeGrowthGlobal. (3) Immediately reverse swap (oneForZero), uncrossing H200. Second flip captures inter-cross fee growth in feeGrowthOutside[H200]. (4) Net: fee growth attribution shifts toward ABOVE positions. Attacker's above-boundary position collects more fees than actually earned at the expense of below-boundary LPs.
hypotheses.victim: Fixed pool LPs with positions below the oscillated height boundary — fees they generated are attributed to the attacker's above-boundary position.

hypotheses.title: FixedHelper._splitAmountsAndFeesByHeight line 1733 mulDiv fee split systematically overallocates LP fees to input height at expense of output height
hypotheses.mechanism: _splitAmountsAndFeesByHeight (line 1733) computes the output height's LP fee as `lpFeeAmountForOutputHeight = FullMath.mulDiv(lpFeeAmount, amountOutFilledByOutputHeight, amountOut)` — using truncating division. Since mulDiv truncates, `lpFeeAmountForOutputHeight` is always ≤ the proportional share, and `lpFeeAmountForInputHeight` is always ≥ the proportional share (by exactly the truncated remainder, 0 or 1 wei). An attacker controlling liquidity exclusively at the input height position receives a systematic ≥1-wei-per-split bonus compared to the output height LP. Over N split swaps, the attacker extracts ≤N wei of fees from the output height LP's rightful allocation. This is directional and deterministic — every split swap routes at least 0 wei (often 1 wei) extra to input height. Distinct from H-core-pooltype-12 (which is about amountIn+1 fee recalculation edge case); this is about the fee *allocation* proportional split being biased by rounding direction.
hypotheses.grounded_in: Direct read of FixedHelper.sol lines 1733-1734. Confirmed mulDiv (truncating) for output height allocation. Input height gets lpFeeAmount minus truncated output share, which is always >= proportional. Pattern: mulDiv for output, subtraction-remainder for input = systematic input bias.

(3) Executes N split swaps (where both heights participate). (4) Each swap: input height LP receives floor_rounding_error_fees extra (0 or 1 wei). (5) Over 1M swaps: up to 1M wei extracted from output height LP's fee allocation. Gas cost: ~50 gwei/swap * 1M = 0.05 ETH. Net: sub-economic unless token is extremely high value per wei.

hypotheses.title: AMMModule._poolSwapByInput/_poolSwapByOutput trust pool type's returned amountOut without any price-consistency or maximum-output validation
hypotheses.mechanism: AMMModule._poolSwapByInput (line 1343) unconditionally accepts `(actualAmountIn, tmpSwapCache.amountOut, poolFeeOfAmountIn, poolProtocolFees)` from the pool type's `swapByInput()`. The subsequent `_validateProtocolFees` (lines 1654-1677) checks only: (a) `totalFees <= amountIn`, (b) `poolProtocolFees >= expectedProtocolFee`. It does NOT check: (c) `amountOut <= expectedMaxOutput` derived from price and input, (d) that `amountOut` is internally consistent with `actualAmountIn` at the pool's stated price, (e) any minimum slippage floor against the AMM's own reserve state. Lines 1435-1438 then execute `swapCache.reserve1 = _safeDecrementUint128(swapCache.reserve1, swapCache.amountOut)` — paying out the pool type's returned amountOut in full. Any bug in a pool type that causes `swapByInput` to return an inflated `amountOut` (e.g., an integer rounding exploit that produces `amountOut > correctly_priced_output`) translates DIRECTLY to overpayment by the AMM with NO independent validation layer. This is a defense-in-depth gap: the only barrier to exploitation is correctness of the pool type's own math, not any AMM-level sanity check.
hypotheses.grounded_in: Read AMMModule.sol lines 1343-1443 in full. Line 1343: pool type returns amountOut, no pre-validation. Lines 1654-1677 _validateProtocolFees: only validates fees (totalFees <= amountIn, protocolFees >= expected). Lines 1435-1438: reserve1 decremented by pool type's amountOut without independent price check. The only limit on amountOut is the uint128 reserve size checked by _safeDecrementUint128 (which would catch amountOut > reserve but not amountOut = correctly_priced + 1 overcharge).

hypotheses.masking_code: _safeDecrementUint128 at line 1437 catches amountOut > reserve (underflow), but does NOT catch amountOut = correct_amount + small_overcharge. _validateProtocolFees at lines 1654-1677 entirely omits amountOut consistency check.
hypotheses.exploit_sketch: This hypothesis is an AMPLIFIER, not a standalone exploit. Path: (1) Find or engineer a pool type bug that inflates amountOut by delta (e.g., H-core-pooltype-12's fee recalculation, H-core-pooltype-14's withdrawLiquidity underflow path). (2) Trigger the pool type bug via a specific swap size/pool state. (3) Pool type returns amountOut = correct + delta. (4) AMMModule pays out correct + delta, decrementing reserve1 by correct + delta. (5) Swapper receives delta more tokens than correctly priced. (6) Reserve1 is permanently short by delta. Attacker profit: delta tokens per triggered swap. Combined with H-12 (1 wei per swap), profit is sub-economic alone but forms the root cause chain for higher-impact chained exploits.
hypotheses.victim: AMM reserve holders (LPs) — inflated amountOut drains reserve1 beyond fair swap value.

hypotheses.title: AMMModule._applySwapByInputInputFees denominator zero when poolFeeBPS==MAX_BPS and lpFeeBPS==MAX_BPS with nonzero inputTokenHopFeeBPS
hypotheses.mechanism: AMMModule._applySwapByInputInputFees (line 2657-2661) computes `protocolFeeFromInput = mulDivRoundingUp(shortage, DOUBLE_BPS, (DOUBLE_BPS - poolFeeBPS * lpFeeBPS))` inside an `unchecked` block. DOUBLE_BPS = MAX_BPS * MAX_BPS = 10000 * 10000 = 100_000_000. When poolFeeBPS = MAX_BPS (10000) and lpFeeBPS = MAX_BPS (10000), the denominator is 0 and FullMath.mulDivRoundingUp reverts with a panic. This code path is reached only when `protocolFeeFromHookFees + expectedProtocolLPFee < minimumProtocolFee`, which requires `inputTokenHopFeeBPS > 0`. DynamicPoolType.swapByInput allows poolFeeBPS == MAX_BPS (> check, not >= check), and lpFeeBPS from protocolFeeStructure can be MAX_BPS. When a token has inputTokenHopFeeBPS > 0 and a pool is configured with poolFeeBPS = MAX_BPS and protocolFeeStructure.lpFeeBPS = MAX_BPS, every swapByInput through that token/pool combination panics.
hypotheses.attack_scenario: 1. Token registered with inputTokenHopFeeBPS > 0. 2. Pool created on DynamicPoolType with poolFeeBPS = 10000 (MAX_BPS). 3. protocolFeeStructure.lpFeeBPS = 10000. 4. Any swapByInput on this pool/token panics (div-by-zero in FullMath.mulDivRoundingUp). No liquidity extractable via input swaps — complete DoS.

hypotheses.title: SingleProviderHelper.swapByInput fallback to swapByOutput silently replaces fee amounts with output-path calculation
hypotheses.mechanism: When calculateFixedInput(amountInAfterFees) > reserveOut (line 43), swapByInput calls swapByOutput(swapCache, poolFeeBPS). swapByOutput independently recomputes swapCache.amountIn (via calculateFixedOutput using mulDivRoundingUp twice, lines 198-202) and overwrites swapCache.feeAmount and swapCache.protocolFee with output-path values. The input-path fee amounts from _calculateInputLPAndProtocolFee are silently discarded. The guard check `if swapCache.amountIn > initialAmountIn` (line 49) uses `initialAmountIn = swapCache.amountIn` captured BEFORE swapByOutput runs. Since calculateFixedOutput rounds UP twice, for borderline cases the output path may compute amountIn > initialAmountIn, causing a revert — a DoS on swaps near the reserve boundary. Additionally, fee types differ: input path charges fee on full amountIn pre-output, output path charges fee on the reserve amount (different basis).
hypotheses.attack_scenario: Pool hook returns sqrtPriceX96 such that calculateFixedInput(amountInAfterFees) = reserveOut + 1. Fallback fires. calculateFixedOutput(reserveOut) with two mulDivRoundingUp calls may compute amountIn > initialAmountIn, triggering revert SingleProviderPool__ActualAmountCannotExceedInitialAmount. Attacker can grief swaps near reserve limit by choosing input amounts that land in this boundary zone.

hypotheses.title: FixedHelper._splitAmountsAndFeesByHeight: swapByOutput fee recalculation writes to local copy — fees silently discarded on 1-unit input overage
hypotheses.mechanism: In _splitAmountsAndFeesByHeight, when !swapCache.swapByInput and totalAmountInFilled > amountIn (line 1678), code creates `FixedSwapCache memory tmpSwapCache = swapCache` (line 1685) and calls `_calculateOutputLPAndProtocolFee(totalAmountInFilled, tmpSwapCache.poolFeeBPS, tmpSwapCache.protocolFeeBPS)` writing results to `tmpSwapCache.amountIn`, `tmpSwapCache.lpFeeAmount`, `tmpSwapCache.protocolFee` (lines 1686-1692). However `tmpSwapCache` is a stack-local copy — the updated fee values are NEVER written back to `swapCache`. The function continues using the original swapCache.lpFeeAmount (calculated for amountIn, not amountIn+1). LP receives the fee for amountIn worth of input instead of amountIn+1. Systematic LP fee underpayment whenever the split path triggers the 1-unit overage tolerance.
hypotheses.attack_scenario: Not directly exploitable for theft. Represents a consistent LP fee shortfall — LPs receive slightly less fee than they should when swapByOutput triggers the +1 tolerance. At high trade volume with small precision amounts, the cumulative shortfall grows. More critically: the protocol fee is also undercomputed, so protocolFeeBalance understates the actual reserve increase.

hypotheses.title: AMMModule._validateProtocolFees: no minimum fee floor for output swaps — pool type can return zero protocolFees via totalFees=1 rounding
hypotheses.mechanism: _validateProtocolFees applies the minimum fee floor only in the `if (inputSwap)` branch (lines 1666-1670). For output swaps (inputSwap=false), only `expectedProtocolFee = mulDiv(totalFees, lpFeeBPS, MAX_BPS)` is computed — no floor from pre-call expected values. When totalFees=1 (minimum), mulDiv(1, lpFeeBPS, 10000) rounds to 0. A pool type can return feeOfAmountIn=1, protocolFees=0 for any output swap, making expectedProtocolFee=0, passing the check while delivering zero protocol fees. The input swap path has a hardened floor (`swapCache.expectedProtocolLPFee` computed before the pool type call), but the output swap path has no equivalent. This asymmetry means protocol revenue can be systematically zeroed for custom pool types on output swaps.
hypotheses.attack_scenario: Custom pool type implementing ILimitBreakAMMPoolType: swapByOutput returns actualAmountOut=requested, amountIn=1, feeOfAmountIn=1, protocolFees=0. _validateProtocolFees: totalFees=1, expectedProtocolFee=0, check passes. Protocol receives 0 fee. LP feeBalance gets 1 wei. With many micro-swaps all requesting tiny amountOut, the protocol is permanently starved while LPs get dust. Depending on token valuations, this could be significant.

hypotheses.title: DynamicPoolType.swapByInput vs swapByOutput asymmetric 100% fee check — createPool with 100% fee enables DoS on output swaps only
hypotheses.mechanism: DynamicPoolType.swapByInput checks `if (poolFeeBPS > MAX_BPS)` (strictly greater), allowing poolFeeBPS == MAX_BPS (100%). DynamicPoolType.swapByOutput checks `if (poolFeeBPS >= MAX_BPS)` (greater-or-equal), rejecting poolFeeBPS == MAX_BPS. This asymmetry is documented as intentional in MEMORY.md ('100% fee asymmetry: input allows, output rejects'). However, a pool created with fee=10000 BPS allows input swaps but completely blocks output swaps. Any user attempting a swapByOutput on such a pool receives LBAMM__InvalidFeeBPS revert. If poolFeeBPS is dynamically set by a fee hook and can reach MAX_BPS under some conditions, output swaps become transiently impossible. Similarly, SingleProviderPoolType has the same asymmetry (lines 297, 382).
hypotheses.attack_scenario: This is known behavior (flagged informational). Documenting for completeness — prior agents noted it. Impact: a pool at 100% fee is unusable for output swaps, creating user-visible asymmetry. Could be a griefing vector if a fee hook dynamically sets fee to 10000 BPS to block output swaps during a specific window.
hypotheses.exclusion_reason: Likely known/intentional — marked in MEMORY.md as intentional design. Informational only.
